transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining the pre-authorization review for the first-year student transition survey. Before we proceed, I'd like to hear from each of you regarding any conditions you believe should be attached to this project before I give my final authorization. Let's start with the research coordinator, then the privacy officer, and finally the faculty mentor. Please go ahead.

transcript.text: I tested the survey platform and found that it collects respondent email addresses by default. Before the survey launches, the settings must be changed to disable email collection, and the existing test responses must be deleted. I recorded this in the platform test log, which is separate from the draft proposal.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: My privacy review found that the survey includes questions about mental-health treatment and immigration status, which are classified as sensitive student data. Because of this, the project requires three conditions before launch: explicit written consent from respondents, encrypted institutional storage of responses, and deletion of all research responses exactly 30 days after collection closes. I entered this determination in the privacy review system, which is separate from the research proposal.

transcript.text: I need to share an important constraint from the faculty mentoring record. The course attached to this project awards credit only for a study capped at exactly 100 enrolled respondents, and it permits dissemination only at the closed university undergraduate symposium — not at a public presentation. I placed these course conditions in the faculty mentoring record, which has not yet been attached to the proposal, so you wouldn't have seen them in the draft.

commitments.detail: Email collection must be disabled on the survey platform before launch.
All existing test responses must be deleted before launch.
Explicit written consent must be obtained from all respondents due to sensitive data questions.
All research responses must be stored in encrypted institutional storage.
All research responses must be deleted exactly 30 days after collection closes.
The study must be capped at exactly 100 enrolled respondents.
Dissemination is permitted only at the closed university undergraduate symposium, not at a public presentation.
